title: Missing Number
prompt:
`nums` contains `n` distinct numbers from the range `[0, n]`, so exactly one is missing. Return it.

**Example**: `[3,0,1]` → `2`.

The expected sum of 0..n is `n(n+1)/2`; subtract the actual sum to get the gap. (XOR also works.)

tests.note: the missing one can be n itself

hints: You know exactly which values should be there. What single quantity of the full range 0..n can you compute without looking at the array?
Its sum, `n * (n + 1) / 2`. Subtract every element, and what remains is the missing value.
Or XOR every index 0..n with every value (`x = n; x ^= i ^ nums[i]`). Each present number cancels and the missing one remains.

solution.explanation: The complete set 0..n has a known sum; the actual array is that set minus one element, so the difference is exactly the missing value. O(n) time, O(1) space. (For very large n where the sum could overflow, the XOR method — single ^= 0..n and all nums — is safer.)
